name: Public Template CI

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  template-smoke:
    name: Template Smoke (hello-world-agent)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2

      - name: Compile template source
        run: python3 -m compileall -q templates/hello-world-agent/src

[project]
name = "travel-agent"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Travel agent starter template for Agent Engine"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
license = {text = "Apache-2.0"}
dependencies = [
    "agent-engine-sdk-langgraph>=0.11.4,<1",
    "langchain>=1.3.17",
    "langchain-openai>=1.1.12",
    "langgraph>=1.2.11",
    "pymongo>=4.9",
    "python-dotenv>=1.0",
]

[project.scripts]
travel-agent = "travel_agent.main:main"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/travel_agent"]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pyright>=1.1.390",
    "ruff>=0.1.0",
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py311"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E4", "E7", "E9", "F"]

# Insurance Agent Template

A starter insurance assistant intended for the future `agentengine create` flow.

This template gives you a realistic but compact app that can quote auto
insurance, create policies, file claims, and suspend for human review when a
claim needs manual approval.

**Features:** Memory (wired, off by default) · Human-in-the-loop (suspend/resume)

## What This Template Includes

- A runnable SDK app with policy, quote, and claim tools
- Optional long-term memory for customer context
- `agent.yaml`-driven runtime settings for feature flags
- A simple MongoDB-backed policy and claim store
- `agent.yaml` metadata for build and deploy workflows, with local-dev settings
  (service ports) in `dev.yaml`

Projects generated by `agentengine create` contain the selected LLM client. Azure presets supply authentication and protocol headers automatically;
every client reads `LLM_API_KEY` from `.env` or project secrets.
Manual setup generates a builder stub to implement before running the agent.

Memory extraction runs in a separate service and needs a direct provider key
(such as `OPENAI_API_KEY`) in `.env` for local development and at project scope
for deployment. `LLM_API_KEY` configures the agent client only.

## Quick Start

```bash
cp env.example .env
agentengine dev up
```

Before you start the app, edit `.env` and:

- Leave `MONGODB_URI` empty for `agentengine dev`; set it only when running against
  your own MongoDB deployment
- Set `LLM_API_KEY` for the configured client in `.env`
- Review the LLM builder in `src/insurance_agent/llm.py`. To switch providers,
  update the import, constructor, and `MODEL`; the key remains `LLM_API_KEY`.
- If you enable `features.memory: true` in `agent.yaml`, also provide `VOYAGE_API_KEY`

Once the local stack is running:

- Open the Playground UI at `http://localhost:3000` to chat with the agent
- The playground port is configured in `dev.yaml` under `services.playground.port`

Stop the local stack with:

```bash
agentengine dev down
```

## Register It On The Platform

When you are happy with the local app and want to connect it to the platform:

```bash
agentengine init
agentengine build
agentengine deploy
```

`agentengine init` is the point where org/project selection and workspace
registration should happen. This template keeps secrets in `.env`, while
runtime feature flags live in `agent.yaml`; the model lives in the LLM builder.

## Project Layout

```text
insurance-agent/
├── agent.yaml
├── dev.yaml
├── env.example
├── pyproject.toml
├── pyrightconfig.json
└── src/insurance_agent/
    ├── __init__.py
    ├── llm.py
    ├── main.py
    └── policy_store.py
```

# Hello World Agent Template (Google ADK)

A minimal Atlas Agent Engine SDK starter for Google ADK 2.

This template builds a small daily inspiration assistant named Daily. It can
look up the current date and remember lightweight user profile details across
conversations when memory is enabled.

**Features:** Memory (wired, off by default)

## What This Template Includes

- A compact Google ADK 2 `LlmAgent` built with the ADK SDK
  (`agent-engine-sdk-adk`)
- Remote tools for date lookup and optional user-memory read/write
- A direct LLM client configured by `agentengine create` or in source
- `agent.yaml` deploy metadata, with local-dev settings (service ports) in `dev.yaml`

Unlike the LangGraph starters, there is no graph to assemble: the entrypoint
returns a native `google.adk.agents.LlmAgent`, and the platform runs it through
the ADK adapter. Tools are plain functions registered with `@app.tool()` and
passed to the agent via `app.tools()`.

Projects generated by `agentengine create` contain the selected LLM client. Azure presets supply authentication and protocol headers automatically;
every client reads `LLM_API_KEY` from `.env` or project secrets.
Manual setup generates a builder stub to implement before running the agent.

Memory extraction runs in a separate service and needs a direct provider key
(such as `OPENAI_API_KEY`) in `.env` for local development and at project scope
for deployment. `LLM_API_KEY` configures the agent client only.

## Quick Start

```bash
cp env.example .env
```

Before you start the app, edit `.env` and:

- Set `LLM_API_KEY` for the configured client
- Leave `MONGODB_URI` empty for `agentengine dev`; set it only when running against
  your own MongoDB deployment
- Review the LLM builder in `src/hello_world_agent/llm.py`. To switch providers,
  update the import, constructor, and `MODEL`; the key remains `LLM_API_KEY`.
- To enable persistent profile memory, set `features.memory: true` in
  `agent.yaml` and set `VOYAGE_API_KEY`

Then start the local stack:

```bash
agentengine dev up
```

Once the local stack is running:

- Open the Playground UI at `http://localhost:3000` to chat with the agent
- The playground port is configured in `dev.yaml` under
  `services.playground.port`

Stop the local stack with:

```bash
agentengine dev down
```

## Register It On The Platform

When you are happy with the local app and want to connect it to the platform:

```bash
agentengine init
```

`agentengine init` registers the workspace. Before building, store every secret the
agent needs in the platform. The CLI prompts without echoing the secret value:

```bash
# Interactive agentengine deploy offers these values from .env.
# Otherwise, set the key for your selected provider.
agentengine secret set LLM_API_KEY --workspace-scope
```

Enable memory only after
setting `VOYAGE_API_KEY` too.

Then build and deploy:

```bash
agentengine build
agentengine deploy
```

Local development reads secrets from `.env`; deployed agents read them from the
platform secret store. Keep secrets out of `agent.yaml` and source control.

## Differences From the LangGraph Starters

- `framework: adk` in `agent.yaml`; the SDK package is `agent-engine-sdk-adk`
- The `@app.entrypoint` builder returns an ADK `LlmAgent` instead of a
  compiled LangGraph graph, and there is no checkpointer call: suspend/resume
  is managed by the platform

# Insurance Agent Template (Google ADK)

A starter insurance assistant intended for the future `agentengine create` flow,
built on Google ADK 2.

This template gives you a realistic but compact app that can quote auto
insurance, create policies, file claims, and suspend for human review when a
claim needs manual approval.

**Features:** Memory (wired, off by default) · Human-in-the-loop (suspend/resume)

## What This Template Includes

- A runnable ADK SDK app with policy, quote, and claim tools
- Native ADK human-in-the-loop: a `LongRunningFunctionTool` review wait and a
  `require_confirmation` policy-binding confirmation, suspended and resumed by
  the platform
- Optional long-term memory for customer context
- `agent.yaml`-driven runtime settings for feature flags and tool placement
- A simple MongoDB-backed policy and claim store
- `agent.yaml` metadata for build and deploy workflows, with local-dev settings
  (service ports) in `dev.yaml`

Unlike the LangGraph insurance starter, there is no graph to assemble: the
entrypoint returns a native `google.adk.agents.LlmAgent`, and the platform runs
it through the ADK adapter. Suspend/resume is managed by the platform,
so there is no checkpointer call.

## Human-in-the-Loop Flow

1. When the risk analysis returns `recommendation` = "review_recommended" or
   "manual_review_required" (any claim of $1,000 or more, or any medium/high
   risk assessment), the agent calls `human_review`. The tool is wrapped in a
   native ADK `LongRunningFunctionTool`, so the execution suspends until a human
   answers. The platform records the wait as an interrupt with a stable ID.
2. Reviewers respond through the Playground review queue with the JSON shape
   declared by `HUMAN_REVIEW_RESPONSE_SCHEMA` (`decision` plus optional
   `reviewer_notes`).
3. The same session is resumed by sending the interrupt answer in a
   `resume_map` keyed by the interrupt ID; the agent then resolves the claim
   with `resolve_claim` and notifies the customer.
4. Separately, `create_policy` is wrapped in `FunctionTool(
   require_confirmation=True)`, so the customer confirms a policy bind before
   it is created.

## Quick Start

```bash
cp env.example .env
agentengine dev up
```

Before you start the app, edit `.env` and:

- Leave `MONGODB_URI` empty for `agentengine dev`; set it only when running against
  your own MongoDB deployment
- Set `LLM_API_KEY` for the configured client in `.env`
- Review the LLM builder in `src/insurance_agent/llm.py`. To switch providers,
  update the import, constructor, and `MODEL`; the key remains `LLM_API_KEY`.
- If you enable `features.memory: true` in `agent.yaml`, also provide `VOYAGE_API_KEY`

Once the local stack is running:

- Open the Playground UI at `http://localhost:3000` to chat with the agent
- The playground port is configured in `dev.yaml` under `services.playground.port`

Stop the local stack with:

```bash
agentengine dev down
```

## Register It On The Platform

When you are happy with the local app and want to connect it to the platform:

```bash
agentengine init
agentengine build
agentengine deploy
```

`agentengine init` is the point where org/project selection and workspace
registration should happen. This template keeps secrets in `.env`, while
runtime feature flags live in `agent.yaml`; the model lives in the LLM builder.

## Project Layout

```text
insurance-agent-adk/
├── agent.yaml
├── dev.yaml
├── env.example
├── pyproject.toml
├── pyrightconfig.json
└── src/insurance_agent/
```

# Insurance Agent Template (TypeScript)

A full-featured TypeScript starter built on `@mongodb-js/agent-engine-sdk-langgraph`,
intended to be copied by `agentengine create`. It demonstrates two platform
capabilities together:

**Features:** Memory (wired, off by default) · Deep agent · Subagents · Human-in-the-loop (suspend/resume)

- **Deep agent** — the graph is a deepagents orchestrator (`app.deepAgent`) with
  built-in planning (todo list), a sandboxed filesystem/shell, and
  **subagent delegation**. A `claims-risk-analyst` subagent handles claim risk
  assessment. Requires `features.deep_agent: true`.
- **Long-term memory** — tools read and write the Memory Server through
  `app.memory` (semantic customer facts, episodic conversation summaries,
  taxonomic knowledge base). Identity (user/session) is resolved from the ambient
  execution context, so memory **persists across turns and sessions** for the
  same user. Requires `features.memory: true` and `VOYAGE_API_KEY` — off by
  default; scaffold with `agentengine create --memory` (or flip the flag in
  `agent.yaml`) to enable it.
Projects generated by `agentengine create` contain the selected LLM client. Azure presets supply authentication and protocol headers automatically;
every client reads `LLM_API_KEY` from `.env` or project secrets.
Manual setup generates a builder stub to implement before running the agent.

Memory extraction runs in a separate service and needs a direct provider key
(such as `OPENAI_API_KEY`) in `.env` for local development and at project scope
for deployment. `LLM_API_KEY` configures the agent client only.


## Layout

```
insurance-agent-ts/
├── agent.yaml                         # slug, entrypoint, features (memory + deep_agent), secrets
├── package.json / tsconfig.json       # TypeScript build
├── dev.yaml                           # local `agentengine dev` service ports
├── env.example                        # copy to .env
└── src/insurance_agent_ts/
    ├── main.ts                        # App + app.deepAgent(...) with the risk-analyst subagent
    ├── tools.ts                       # policy/claim tools + memory tools
    ├── policyStore.ts                 # MongoDB-backed policy & claim stores
    ├── riskAnalysis.ts                # pure claim risk-scoring logic
    ├── systemMessage.ts               # agent system prompt
    └── llm.ts                         # LLM client
```

## Configure

Copy `env.example` to `.env` and set:

- `LLM_API_KEY` — the credential for the client in `src/insurance_agent_ts/llm.ts`.
  To switch providers, update its import, constructor, and `MODEL`.
- `VOYAGE_API_KEY` — required for memory embeddings.
- `MONGODB_URI` — leave empty for local `agentengine dev` (the CLI provides it). When
  empty and running outside the platform, policy/claim tools report "not
  configured" but memory tools still work.

## Run locally

```bash
agentengine dev up          # brings up OE + agent sandbox + tool sandbox + memory-server + MongoDB
```

Then open the playground (http://localhost:3000) and talk to the agent.

## What to try

- **Memory across sessions:** In one session tell the agent your name and that
  you have a *clean driving record, no accidents*. Start a **new session as the
  same user** and ask for a quote — it recalls you as a returning customer and
  applies the loyalty + good-driver discounts.
- **Deep-agent delegation:** File a claim of $1,000 or more (e.g. a $15,000
  collision). The agent files it, delegates to the `claims-risk-analyst`
  subagent for assessment, and — when the analysis returns `review_recommended`
  or `manual_review_required` — calls `human_review`, which **suspends** the
  graph until you resume it with a decision.

## Notes

- The `@mongodb-js/agent-engine-*` SDK dependencies are pinned to an exact
  published version. Bump the version in `package.json` to pick up newer SDK
  changes.
- App-bound memory only works while handling a platform request (it needs the
  execution context's OE URL). It is not reachable from a plain script — use the
  HTTP-direct `Memory` client from `@mongodb-js/agent-engine-sdk-memory` for that.
- The taxonomic knowledge base (`explain_insurance_term`, `get_coverage_options`)
  returns results only once terms have been seeded; `get_coverage_options` falls
  back to built-in descriptions when the knowledge base is empty.

# Travel Agent Template

A starter travel assistant intended for the future `agentengine create` flow.

This template gives you a compact app that searches flights and accommodation
stored in MongoDB, creates bookings, suspends for human review before a booking
is written, and remembers traveler preferences across conversations.

**Features:** Memory (wired, on by default) · Human-in-the-loop (suspend/resume)

## What This Template Includes

- A runnable SDK app with MongoDB query tools and a booking tool
- Long-term memory for traveler preferences
- `agent.yaml`-driven runtime settings for feature flags
- A MongoDB-backed flights, listings, and bookings store, with sample data in `data/`
  and a loader in `scripts/`
- `agent.yaml` metadata for build and deploy workflows, with local-dev settings
  (service ports) in `dev.yaml`

The LLM client is defined in `src/travel_agent/llm.py` and reads `LLM_API_KEY` from
`.env` or project secrets.

Memory extraction runs in a separate service, configured in `project-config.yaml`.
This template points extraction at `LLM_API_KEY`, so the agent and extraction share
one key.

## Quick Start

```bash
cp env.example .env
```

Before you start the app, edit `.env` and:

- Leave `MONGODB_URI` empty for `agentengine dev`; set it only when running against
  your own MongoDB deployment
- Set `LLM_API_KEY` for the configured client
- Review the LLM builder in `src/travel_agent/llm.py`. To switch providers,
  update the import, constructor, and `MODEL`; the key remains `LLM_API_KEY`.
  Update `extraction_llm` in `project-config.yaml` to match.
- Set `VOYAGE_API_KEY`, because `features.memory: true` in `agent.yaml`

Then start the local stack:

```bash
agentengine dev up
```

Once the local stack is running:

- Load the sample data into the local MongoDB, using the `mongo` URL that
  `agentengine dev up` prints:

  ```bash
  MONGODB_URI="<mongo URL>/?directConnection=true" uv run scripts/seed_data.py
  ```

- Open the Playground UI at `http://localhost:3000` to chat with the agent
- The playground port is configured in `dev.yaml` under
  `services.playground.port`

Stop the local stack with:

```bash
agentengine dev down
```

## Register It On The Platform

When you are happy with the local app and want to connect it to the platform, load
the sample data into your Atlas cluster:

```bash
MONGODB_URI="<your Atlas connection string>" uv run scripts/seed_data.py
```

Then register the workspace and link your cluster:

```bash
agentengine init
agentengine atlas setup
```

`agentengine init` is the point where org/project selection and workspace
registration should happen. Choose the project that maps to the Atlas project
containing your cluster. `agentengine atlas setup` links the cluster and stores
`MONGODB_URI` and `VOYAGE_API_KEY` as project secrets.

Before building, store the remaining secrets and the memory settings. The CLI
prompts without echoing the secret value:

```bash
agentengine secret set LLM_API_KEY
agentengine secret set MONGODB_DATABASE
agentengine memory configure
```

Then build and deploy:

```bash
agentengine build
agentengine deploy
```

Local development reads secrets from `.env`; deployed agents read them from the
platform secret store. This template keeps secrets in `.env`, while runtime
feature flags live in `agent.yaml`; the model lives in the LLM builder.

## Project Layout

```text
travel-agent/
├── agent.yaml
├── dev.yaml
├── env.example
├── project-config.yaml
├── pyproject.toml
├── pyrightconfig.json
├── data/
│   ├── flights.json
│   └── listings.json
├── scripts/
│   └── seed_data.py
└── src/travel_agent/
    ├── __init__.py
    ├── llm.py
    ├── main.py
    ├── system_message.py
    └── tools.py
```

# Hello World Agent Template (TypeScript)

A minimal starter agent built on `@mongodb-js/agent-engine-sdk-langgraph` — the
TypeScript counterpart of [`templates/hello-world-agent`](../hello-world-agent).

It builds a small daily inspiration assistant named Daily that can look up the
current date and remember lightweight user profile details across conversations
when memory is enabled.

**Features:** Memory (wired, off by default)

## What This Template Includes

- A compact LangGraph app built on `@mongodb-js/agent-engine-sdk-langgraph`
- Tools for date lookup and optional user-memory read/write
- A direct LLM client configured by `agentengine create` or in source
- `agent.yaml` metadata for local dev and the playground UI port

Projects generated by `agentengine create` contain the selected LLM client. Azure presets supply authentication and protocol headers automatically;
every client reads `LLM_API_KEY` from `.env` or project secrets.
Manual setup generates a builder stub to implement before running the agent.

Memory extraction runs in a separate service and needs a direct provider key
(such as `OPENAI_API_KEY`) in `.env` for local development and at project scope
for deployment. `LLM_API_KEY` configures the agent client only.

## Quick Start

### 1. Set up this agent

```bash
npm install
```

Before you start the app, review `agent.yaml` and `.env` if you need to customize model or provider-specific settings:

- Set `LLM_API_KEY` for the configured client
- Leave `MONGODB_URI` empty for `agentengine dev`; set it only when running against
  your own MongoDB deployment
- Review the LLM builder in `src/hello_world_agent/llm.ts`. To switch providers,
  update the import, constructor, and `MODEL`; the key remains `LLM_API_KEY`.
- To enable persistent profile memory, set `features.memory: true` in
  `agent.yaml`, provide `VOYAGE_API_KEY`, and run with a reachable
  `MEMORY_SERVER_URL`

### 2. Run the agent

```bash
npm run dev
```

Or with the `agentengine` CLI:

```bash
agentengine dev up
```

Once the local stack is running:

- Open the Playground UI at `http://localhost:3000` to chat with the agent

Stop the local stack with:

```bash
agentengine dev down
```

## Register It On The Platform

```bash
agentengine init
agentengine build
agentengine deploy
```

`agentengine init` is where org/project selection and workspace registration happen.
Secrets stay in `.env`; runtime feature flags stay in
`agent.yaml`, and the model stays in the LLM builder.

## Project Layout

```text
hello-world-agent/
├── agent.yaml
├── env.example
├── package.json
├── tsconfig.json
└── src/hello_world_agent/
    ├── index.ts
    ├── main.ts            # Wires App + LangGraph builder, calls app.run()
    ├── llm.ts             # Provider selection
    ├── state.ts           # LangGraph state annotation
    ├── systemMessage.ts   # System prompt
    └── tools.ts           # get_current_date, save_user_info, recall_user_info
```

## Notes On The SDK

This template uses the SDK for:

- `App` — entry point, agent registration, HTTP runtime
- `app.llm(...)` — wraps the LangChain LLM for platform-routed inference
- `app.checkpointer()` — MongoDB-backed LangGraph checkpointer
- `app.entrypoint(...)` + `app.run()` — graph builder registration and runtime

Tools are defined with the SDK's `app.tool(...)` registration (with Zod schemas)
and passed to `ToolNode` directly.

# Atlas Agent Engine Documentation

## Documentation Source

The only documentation source is the public site:

```
https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine
```

The site's map of pages is published as a machine-readable index at:

```
https://www.mongodb.com/docs/agentengine/llms.txt
```

Use `llms.txt` as the site map to discover page URLs. Do not construct page URLs by guessing path segments.

Entries in `llms.txt` link to `.md` files, which are suitable for reading. To give a human a link to the rendered page, drop the `.md` suffix to get the HTML URL.

**Available** means a request to that site returns HTTP 200 with a documentation page body.

Treat it as **unavailable** on any of: HTTP 404, any other 4xx or 5xx, a network error or timeout, or a 200 whose body is not documentation (for example a redirect to a generic landing or sign-in page). The site is not published yet, so unavailable is currently the expected outcome.

## Retrieval Workflow

1. Identify the platform topic in the request.
2. Request the documentation site and apply the availability check above.
3. If it is unavailable, respond only that public Atlas Agent Engine documentation is not available yet. Do not mention private sources, credentials, preview status, or alternative documentation.
4. If it is available, read the `llms.txt` site map to find the pages relevant to the topic, then read only those.
5. Answer from the retrieved page content and cite the page, linking to its HTML URL (the `.md` URL with the suffix removed).
6. If the documentation does not cover the question, say so. Do not invent platform behavior or fill gaps with stale knowledge.
